Special Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
Joint REGULAR Meeting
WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 18, 2010
6:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S.HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 or by email at least 72 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24. Council meetings are archived and available for viewing. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings.
A full City Council agenda packet with backup information is available at City Hall, at the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library (157 Stevens Ave.), and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item and that are received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

Special Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
Special Council Meeting
Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority
MINUTES
JOINT SPECIAL MEETING
Wednesday, August 18, 2010
06:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers, 635 S. Highway 101, Solana Beach, California
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
MOTION: Moved by and seconded by .
Motion carried unanimously.
Present:
Nichols, Campbell, Heebner, Kellejian, and Roberts.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Johanna N. Canlas, City Attorney
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Wende Protzman, Dir. Admin. Services/Deputy City Mgr
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director
Tina Christiansen, Comm. Dev. Dir.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer
FLAG SALUTE:
Wende Protzman, Deputy City Manager, led the flag salute.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Kellejian.
Motion carried unanimously.
C.
STAFF REPORTS:
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk
C.1.
November 2, 2010 General Municipal Election - Consideration of Facts. (File 430-20)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Review the Certification of Facts and choose an option:
a.
Adopt Resolution 2010-131 appointing the nominees to elected offices, or
b.
Elect to hold the November 2, 2010 General Municipal Election as called.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item stating that there were options for consideration and that the cancellation of an election had been done once before in 2008.
Jack Hegenauer said that a few years ago he considered running if the incumbants did not run, that elections were not about poplularity, that everyone lived in a participatory democracy, and that everyone had an opportunity to run for office.
Deputy Mayor Heebner said that the public had shared similar comments with her that Mr. Hegenauer stated, that nothing had changed since the last time this action was taken, that there was a period of time to run for office, and that she supported the cancellation of the election and appointment of the nominees.
Councilmember Kellejian said that there was a disadvantage to a write-in candidate since even a write-in canidadate's name would not appear on the ballot and there would not be a candidate statement, that the City Clerk pointed out in 2008 when asked that there was a pointed out in 2008 there was a shorter time period for a write-in candidate's campaign making it difficult to get their name out and win, that there had been ample time to come forward to run, that there were public notices in four languages, that there would be a savings of $10,000, and that there is a lot of Staff time involved in an election which would result in more savings.
Councilmember Roberts said he agreed with the comments and that the public had shared thorugh emailed and letters their support of the action.
Councilmember Nichols said that this occured two years ago and that he supported it then and would support it again.
Mayor Campbell stated that he appreciated all the emails and notes received and Council's comments, that is did not favor it two years ago because he considered the write-in period a part of the democratic process, and that for that reason he was going to vote the same as before and would not support the action to make appointments and cancel the election.
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Kellejian to officially appoint Thomas M. Campbell and Mike Nichols to the offices of Councilmember and cancel the November 2, 2010 General Municipal Election. Appointments will take place December 2010 for the beginning of their newly appointed terms (Dec. 2010-Dec. 2014).
Motion carried 4/1
(Noes: Campbell.)
ADJOURN:
Mayor Campbell adjourned the meeting at 6:12 p.m.
_____________________________ Approved: November 10, 2010
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
